title: Objects and destructuring
description:
Write three functions:

```javascript
function mergeSettings(defaults, user) { }   // a new object: defaults overridden by user; neither input changes
function invert(obj) { }                      // swap keys and values: { a: "x" } becomes { x: "a" }
function summary({ name, age, city = "unknown", ...rest }) { }
```

`summary` returns a string like `"Ada (36) from London, 2 more fields"`. When `age` is missing, leave out ` (36)`; the count is the number of other fields, with `field` for 1 and `fields` otherwise; when there are none, leave out the comma part.

`mergeSettings` also merges one level deeper: if both have a plain object (not an array) under the same key, such as `colors`, the result has both sets of inner properties.
hints: `Object.assign(defaults, user)` writes into `defaults`; `{ ...defaults, ...user }` builds a new object.
`...rest` in the parameter collects every property not named before it; `Object.keys(rest).length` counts them.
